subject: Dedicated capacity: KV cache and quantization sizing for Galileo POC
messages:
From: Maria Delgado <maria@galileo.health>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC sizing: long context & quantization questions

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We want to scope a 6-week POC for a clinical assistant that needs to keep ~12k token patient context (notes + prior messages) and typically returns 200-800 tokens per response. A few details:

- Expected concurrency: peak 60 concurrent sessions (interactive clinicians), average 20 sustained.
- QPS: bursts up to ~120 QPS for short windows.
- Model preference: evaluating two variants — an in-house open model we call "galileo-70b-rc" (architecturally similar to other ~70B decoders), and a cheaper 13B family variant.
- We are open to quantization (int8/4-bit) if it won't break performance for our clinical prompts.
- Security: Dedicated capacity behind our VPC is required.

Can you provide an initial sizing matrix (per-model GPU footprint, recommended GPU type, and how KV cache and quantization affect the number of GPUs we should reserve)? Attached is a sample inference profile with payload sizes and traffic patterns.

Thanks,
Maria
Maria Delgado
CTO, Galileo Health
attachments: galileo_inference_profile.csv (csv)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Delgado <maria@galileo.health>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC sizing: long context & quantization questions

Maria — thanks for the profile, this is helpful. Quick clarifying Qs before I run a detailed calc:

1) When you say 12k token context, is that the typical prefix included in every request (i.e., always cached) or a rolling history where average per-request prefix is closer to 6–8k?
2) For the 70B class model, are you expecting to run it in fp16-only or are you comfortable with int8-int8 quantized weights for the bulk of traffic? We should know whether to plan for kernel-level fp16 activation paths versus int8 weight paths.
3) Any strict latency SLO per interactive session? (e.g., <300ms first-token, <1.5s tail for 200 token responses)

Back-of-envelope notes while we wait:
- KV cache is the big driver for long contexts: quantizing weights reduces model parameter residency, but KV cache (k/v activations) is stored in float16 or bf16 by the runtime and does not shrink with weight quantization.
- For a ~70B decoder with ~80 transformer layers and 128 head-dim-ish layout, rough KV cache per token is on the order of ~0.7–1.0 MB/token (this includes keys+values across layers). For 12k tokens, that’s ~8.4–12 GB of KV memory per concurrent session.
- For a 13B family model the same calculation yields ~0.12–0.2 MB/token → ~1.4–2.4 GB per 12k-token session.
- Model weight residency: fp16 70B ≈ 135–150 GB (multi-GPU sharded); quantized int8 profiles reduce GPU-resident weight working set significantly and can enable single-GPU serving for smaller models; however, the KV cache memory remains the dominant factor with long contexts.

I’ll run a matrix for H100-80GB vs A100-80GB (and a cheaper 48GB class if you want cost options) and share recommended reserved sizes. Marcus and I will coordinate on pricing.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: POC sizing: long context & quantization questions

Team — forwarding Maria's profile. Immediate ask: a pragmatic dedicated cluster recommendation for a 6-week POC (target start Nov 1) that meets the following:
- Support 60 concurrent sessions at peak, avg 20 sustained
- 12k token context assumed worst-case for planning
- Maintain interactive latencies: <500ms first-token, <2.5s for 400–800 token responses at p95
- Provide a cost+capacity tradeoff for: fp16 70B, int8-qualified 70B, and a 13B variant (quantized)

My initial sizing notes (back-of-envelope):
- 70B fp16 path: KV cache dominates. If KV ~= 0.9 MB/token, 12k tokens → ~10.8 GB/session. For 60 concurrent sessions that is ~648 GB of KV state total. You can't shard KV across hosts cheaply at request time; you need headroom on every serving GPU for active sessions pinned there.
- Practically, with H100-80GB boxes using multi-instance (MIG-like logical pods) and our runtime, we can fit ~4–6 concurrent long-context sessions per GPU if we keep model weights sharded across a small pool and rely on request routing to pins. That implies ~12–16 GPUs to support 60 concurrent sessions for 70B fp16.
- With int8 quantized weights (weights quantized but activations/buffers remain 2 bytes), weight residency drops meaningfully and allows more flexible placement and slightly higher concurrency per GPU, but KV cache still limits packing. Expect ~10–12 GPUs for int8-70B (best-case).
- 13B quantized: KV per-session ~2 GB at 12k tokens → for 60 concurrent sessions ~120 GB KV. With int8 weights, a single 80GB GPU can host multiple 13B shards and handle ~8–12 sessions depending on latency SLO. Conservatively plan 4–6 GPUs for the 13B path.

Action items for Rohan: can you validate these ballpark concurrency numbers against runtime memory headroom model and give us a recommended Dedicated SKU (H100-80GB vs A100-80GB vs 48GB alternative) and expected reserved GPU count? Please include failure/fallback guidance (e.g., can we fallback to 13B if 70B capacity saturates) and warm-cache considerations (prefix caching per clinician session).

Marcus — I'll need pricing delta to feed to Maria once Rohan confirms.

Thanks — EV

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Delgado <maria@galileo.health>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 17 Oct 2026 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC sizing: long context & quantization questions — proposal and next steps

Maria — attaching a concise dedicated proposal and the KV cache calculation workbook. Summary below; see attached PDF for pricing and a 2-option commitment (conservative vs cost-optimized).

Summary (short):
- Recommendation (conservative / low-risk): 14 x H100-80GB GPUs in a Dedicated cluster. Reasoning: aim to support 60 concurrent long-context sessions for the 70B fp16 path with 20% headroom for autoscaling and buffer for warm caches. This provides ~4–5 long-context sessions/GPU effective packing after accounting for weight shards and runtime buffers.
- Recommendation (cost-optimized): 10 x H100-80GB GPUs running int8-quantized 70B for the bulk of daytime traffic + 4 x A100-80GB for a fallback pool. Expect slightly higher p95 latency for tails but a ~25% reduction in committed cost versus the conservative option.
- 13B path (if you choose a cheaper model): 4 x A100-80GB (quantized) for the baseline POC. This brings monthly committed GPU hours down ~60% and still meets interactive SLOs for most clinician flows.

Key technical notes:
- KV cache does not compress with weight quantization. The dominant driver for long-context capacity is how many concurrent sessions you can pin per GPU given KV size per session. For 12k tokens we assume ~0.9 MB/token for 70B; workbook has layer-head assumptions that produce this number.
- Warm-cache strategy: pin active clinician sessions to the same serving workers to preserve KV cache across requests and reduce recomputation. For the POC, expect a ~20–30% effective reduction in token work if clinicians re-use sessions.
- Fallbacks: runtime can route to the 13B pool at capacity spill to preserve availability. We recommend an automatic A/B routing policy during the POC so we can monitor regen quality vs latency tradeoffs.

Next steps:
1) Approve which commitment option you want (conservative vs cost-optimized vs 13B fallback).
2) Sign the attached POC SOW and dedicated reservation (DocuSign link in PDF).
3) We’ll schedule a joint runbook call (Rohan + engineering) to validate network/VPC peering and KMS for keys prior to provisioning.

Attachments: rdw_dedicated_proposal_v1.pdf (proposal & cost table), calc_kv_cache.xlsx (workbook with layer/head assumptions and per-session memory calc)

Happy to hop on a call tomorrow to walk the numbers.

—Evelyn
